bugs.title: Handle invalid grub config entries due to os-prober defaulting unidentified file system types

blockers.summary: The reviewer (juliank) says the problem has not been reproduced and understood from the boot side, so it is unclear the patch is correct. He also notes the original hanging-mount bug was later fixed differently, with mount namespaces, which may make this change unnecessary or conflicting.

The 'Where problems could occur' section is factually wrong. It says os-prober is disabled by default, but it is enabled automatically when other OSes are detected at install time. The regression assessment must be redone.

The regression analysis does not say what the fuseblk fallback path actually does or which real filesystems depend on it. Removing it for all unrecognised filesystems may stop os-prober detecting legitimate OSes (for example NTFS or other types grub-probe can't identify), and this has not been assessed.

The description says the earlier hanging-mount fix is in Resolute but not in Noble and Jammy, and that the newer os-prober should be backported there after this SRU. The dependency between the releases and the ordering of uploads is unresolved. The target series and the patch's applicability to each are unclear.

The test plan only reproduces the LVM snapshot case. It has no step that verifies the fix after upgrading, and no regression test that other filesystems (for example NTFS or other OSes) are still detected.

comments.author: dgadomski
comments.body: Thanks Arif, I've uploaded it.

blockers.summary: The upload to jammy-proposed was rejected from the queue as 'languishing for over a month', so the fix is not in -proposed and must be re-uploaded before anything can be verified or released.

The backported patch changes the meaning of rados_connect_timeout=0 from 'use the default' to 'no timeout / wait forever'. The charm-glance context sets the value to 0, so existing deployments could change behaviour or hang after the update. This regression risk is not assessed or documented in the SRU.

The test plan is confusing and inconsistent. It does not clearly state the expected failover behaviour, and the 'disable the default backend, i.e. cinder' step contradicts the ceph/swift backend setup. The reviewer asked for this to be clarified, and no revision has been posted.
The Impact section is unclear about what the bug is and why it matters. The reviewer asked for it to be improved, and no update has been posted.

The 'Where problems could occur' section does not mention the behaviour change for values of 0 and below zero, nor the effect on existing deployments with a configured or default timeout. It also never explains that the timeout is applied through Ceph client options.

The upstream fix is split across two commits. The first only deprecates the option and the second restores it with a changed value semantic. The bug is referenced as 'Related-Bug' on the second commit. It is unclear that both commits are included in the SRU, and the test results come from PPA autopkgtests only, with no functional verification of the timeout.

comments.author: whershberger
comments.body:
There are two standing issues with these patches:

- get_global_pool_hard_max_size parses /proc/sys/vm/max_map_count incorrectly, resulting in the default value being used unconditionally
- The default value returned by get_global_pool_hard_max_size is UINT_MAX; a better/conservative choice would be the kernel's default max_map_count (65530)

We've submitted upstream patches to resolve both of these issues; neither have been merged to qemu's master yet.

https://lists.gnu.org/archive/html/qemu-devel/2026-10/msg04337.html
